Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most of it was given by mail, but some infomations were a bit unclear from the university´s site. For example who to contact before in regards to different questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of help through the school´s student counsellors. They provided me with help to find accomodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was tough. I didnt have accomodation the first month and had to live in Airbnbs and hotels. I recommend to start looking for accomodations way before starting the exchange. I ended up living in a student dorm provided by the uni after my situation couldnt get solved. It was pure luck I got the accomodation tho. I recommend writing messages to landlords in french and also lie about the length of your stay. I found it hard to lie about which led me to look for accomodation in 2 months. (1 month before and 1 month while the exchange had started)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It´s nice. I liked the walk from the student residence chapou. To be honest the student residents offered by the school are quite depressing, very small isolated and unpractical. On the other hand they are cheap and often have a kitchen per room which was really convient. I lived in a dorm where there was a cockroach desinfection every second week or so which was a pain in the ass. So think dearly about the tradeoff between cheap housing and more expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course registration can be a bit stressful, especially when coming from Copenhagen. In the first 3 weeks or so after the intro days you are able to attend all courses to checkout whatever you like and then choose up untill the deadline in the end of the three weeks. Some courses have a limited number of seats, so the uni admits students by their grade average from their home uni.  I messed up badly in the beginning by choosing courses that werent available for the autumn semester which led the first weeks to be very stressful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student councils and mostly other students. Remember to ask around.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Almost. I tried to register for a course I hadnt got preapproved by the home uni, hoping for the course to getting preapproved. I didnt get the course preapproved which led me to some merit problems. But the home university accepted that I took fewer points.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: 1. semester means autumn, 2. means spring. I would advice calling the host university to be sure you have understood everything correctly, so your OLA is done months before the exchange.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was quite tough studying at TSE. In my opinion the courses were way to demanding considering many of them were 2 ECTS and 5 ECTS. I have taken courses in economics at KU that were less demanding than those for 2 ECTS at TSE. I found many of the courses quite uninteresting and really bad taught. Course material is often bad.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: unnecessarily hard. A couple of them have a regulated level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite different. Holdundervisninger are mandatory and must be attended otherwise you can´t attend the exams. The course online rooms are often very unstructured and hard to get around.

questions.answer: Couldnt find accomodation so that ended up being expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Hmmm groceries are quite expensive in the city supermarkets. I recommend to stay away from Casinos! Buy vegetables at the markets in the weekend, that will save you a lot of money.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many offers from sport to trips and partying.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Check out ESN Toulouse, they have a event calender every month. Really nice offers.
The school offer many sport teams you can choose but remember the date of the deadline of signing up for the teams.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
There is a lot to do in Toulouse, especially in the summer.
In the summer there are:
Street / market parties around the city which is a bit like distortion just in a southern french way.
Live music in the streets and concerts in parks.
Hiking in the pyrenees
Go to nearby cities; Lourdes, Albi and Cacasonne
Drink wine/beers in the cosy bars around town.
Go for a walk at canal de brienne or the botanic garden.
